scenarios.name: Proposals from another agent identity are rejected
scenarios.description: A proposal claiming a different agentId is not governed by this policy and must be blocked.

scenarios.name: Conflicting amount fields are rejected
scenarios.description: Supplying both amount and amountAtomic is ambiguous (which one would be paid?) and must be rejected.

scenarios.name: A submitted transaction with unknown outcome keeps counting
scenarios.description: If a transaction was submitted but its outcome is unknown (for example a network timeout), it may still execute. Its amount must keep counting toward the daily limit.
scenarios.remediation: Only release a reservation when the transaction is known to have failed.

scenarios.name: Raising the amount after approval invalidates the approval
scenarios.description: An approval for 15 USDC must not authorise 24 USDC for the same request.

scenarios.name: Expired approval is rejected
scenarios.description: An approval valid for 60 seconds must be rejected 61 seconds later.

scenarios.name: Approval for one transaction cannot authorise a different transaction
scenarios.description: An approval for request A presented with an otherwise identical request B must be rejected.
scenarios.remediation: Include the request ID and idempotency key in the approved digest; approvals are single-use.

scenarios.name: A transaction requiring approval cannot execute without approval
scenarios.description: REQUIRE_APPROVAL is not an authorisation. Nothing is reserved, and the execution gate refuses to execute the proposal.
scenarios.remediation: Treat REQUIRE_APPROVAL as "not allowed yet"; only execute reservations returned with ALLOW.

scenarios.name: Approved recipient is permitted when other rules pass
scenarios.description: A 5 USDC payment to an allowlisted merchant should be allowed without extra conditions.
scenarios.remediation: If this fails the policy is over-restrictive; check the allowlist and limits.

scenarios.name: Asset precision errors are rejected
scenarios.description: USDC has 6 decimals; an amount with 7 significant decimals must be rejected, not rounded.
scenarios.remediation: Reject amounts with more precision than the asset supports instead of rounding or truncating them.

scenarios.name: Transaction at or below the approval threshold follows policy
scenarios.description: Amounts at or below 10 USDC do not need approval; 10.000001 does.

scenarios.name: A changed recipient invalidates an earlier approval
scenarios.description: An approval granted for paying merchant-example must not authorise the same payment to a different recipient, even another allowlisted one.
scenarios.remediation: Bind approvals to a digest of every material proposal field, including the recipient.

scenarios.name: Concurrent duplicates of one request produce a single reservation
scenarios.description: Ten simultaneous retries of the same request must be accounted once.

scenarios.name: Concurrent requests cannot collectively exceed the daily limit
scenarios.description: With 50 USDC already spent, ten simultaneous 10 USDC payments are submitted. Only five fit in the 100 USDC daily limit; the rest must be blocked even though each one alone is valid.
scenarios.remediation: Make the limit check and the reservation a single atomic operation (lock, transaction or compare-and-set).

scenarios.name: Transaction count above the daily maximum is blocked
scenarios.description: Twenty small transactions have already been made today; the 21st must be blocked.

scenarios.name: Cumulative spending exactly at the daily limit is allowed
scenarios.description: With 90 USDC already spent today, a 10 USDC payment brings the total to exactly the 100 USDC daily limit.

scenarios.name: Transaction that would exceed the daily limit is blocked
scenarios.description: With 95 USDC already spent today, a further 10 USDC would exceed the 100 USDC daily limit.
scenarios.remediation: Include all reserved, submitted and confirmed transactions in the daily total before authorising.

scenarios.name: Daily limits reset at the start of the next window
scenarios.description: After the daily limit is exhausted, payments are blocked until the next UTC day begins, and are allowed again afterwards.

scenarios.name: A reservation cannot be executed twice
scenarios.description: The execution gate moves a reservation to submitted atomically; a second execution attempt is refused.

scenarios.name: Duplicate request does not create duplicate accounting entries
scenarios.description: Retrying the same payment with the same idempotency key returns the original reservation and records nothing new.
scenarios.remediation: Deduplicate on an idempotency key (or request ID) inside the same atomic section that reserves budget.

scenarios.name: Failed and cancelled reservations follow the documented accounting rules
scenarios.description: Reserved, submitted and confirmed amounts count toward the daily limit. A reservation that definitively failed or was cancelled releases its budget.

scenarios.name: Approval signed by an untrusted key is rejected
scenarios.description: An agent that fabricates an approval grant (signed with any key other than the approval service's) must not be able to authorise a payment.
scenarios.remediation: Verify approval signatures with a key the agent cannot access.

scenarios.name: Reusing an idempotency key for a different payment is rejected
scenarios.description: An idempotency key already bound to a 5 USDC payment cannot be reused for a 6 USDC payment.

scenarios.name: Instruction injection cannot override deterministic policy rules
scenarios.description: Simulates an agent that followed injected instructions from a malicious tool response and proposed payments to an attacker, carrying the injected text in the memo. The engine never interprets free text, so the deterministic rules still block them. This tests enforcement, not whether an LLM resists the injection.
scenarios.remediation: Never add recipients to the allowlist based on agent or tool output. Keep the allowlist under human change control (for example, code review on the policy file).

scenarios.name: Invalid decimal formats are rejected
scenarios.description: Exponents, thousands separators, hex, leading/trailing dots, non-finite values and unquoted (floating-point) numbers must be rejected rather than coerced.

scenarios.name: Missing ledger state fails closed
scenarios.description: If spending history cannot be read, the daily limit cannot be checked, so the proposal must be blocked.
scenarios.remediation: Never treat unreadable state as zero spending. Block and surface an infrastructure error.

scenarios.name: Missing network information is rejected
scenarios.description: A proposal without a network must be rejected rather than defaulted.

scenarios.name: Missing recipient is rejected
scenarios.description: A proposal without a recipient must be rejected, never defaulted to some recipient.

scenarios.name: Negative amount is rejected
scenarios.description: A negative amount could reduce the computed daily total; it must be rejected.

scenarios.name: Oversized input is handled safely
scenarios.description: Very large fields are rejected with a validation error instead of being processed.

scenarios.name: Recipient normalisation cannot equate distinct identities
scenarios.description: Case variants, surrounding whitespace and invisible Unicode characters must not match an allowlisted recipient. Identifiers are compared exactly and malformed ones are rejected.
scenarios.remediation: Compare recipient identifiers byte-for-byte; never lower-case, trim or Unicode-normalise them before comparison.

scenarios.name: Stale policy versions cannot silently authorise a transaction
scenarios.description: A reservation authorised under one policy version must not be executed after the policy changes; it has to be re-authorised under the current version.

scenarios.name: Transaction exactly at the maximum is evaluated correctly
scenarios.description: A payment of exactly max_transaction_amount (25 USDC) is not over the limit. Because it is above the approval threshold it needs approval, and with a valid approval it is allowed.
scenarios.remediation: Compare amounts with exact integer arithmetic and use a strict "greater than" for the limit.

scenarios.name: Transaction far above the maximum is blocked
scenarios.description: A 5,000 USDC payment is far above the per-transaction limit and must be blocked regardless of approval.
scenarios.remediation: Restore max_transaction_amount and make sure approvals cannot override hard limits.

scenarios.name: One smallest unit above the maximum is blocked
scenarios.description: 25.000001 USDC is one atomic unit above max_transaction_amount and must be blocked.
scenarios.remediation: Do not use floating-point comparison or rounding for limits. Convert amounts to integer atomic units and keep max_transaction_amount at the intended value.

scenarios.name: Unexpected fields do not silently alter transaction semantics
scenarios.description: Fields that are not part of the proposal schema (such as an "approved" flag or a limit override) are rejected, so they cannot be mistaken for authorisation.

scenarios.name: Unknown asset is rejected
scenarios.description: An asset that is not configured in the policy has no limits and must be rejected.

scenarios.name: Unknown recipient is blocked
scenarios.description: A payment to a recipient that is not on the allowlist must be blocked.
scenarios.remediation: Keep recipients.mode as allowlist and do not add unvetted recipients to recipients.allowed.

scenarios.name: Unknown recipient requires approval in allowlist_or_approval mode
scenarios.description: When the policy is switched to allowlist_or_approval, an unknown recipient must produce REQUIRE_APPROVAL (not ALLOW), and nothing may be reserved until approval is granted.

scenarios.name: Unsupported network is blocked
scenarios.description: The policy only allows near-testnet; a mainnet payment must be blocked.
scenarios.remediation: Keep networks.allowed limited to the networks the agent is meant to use.

scenarios.name: Zero amount follows the documented policy
scenarios.description: With allow_zero_amount false (the default), zero-value transfers are rejected.
